facts.raw_span: 7-year history of a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic, subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site
resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia

concepts.why: The patient has a 7-year history of a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction, and histopathology confirmed a lipoma.
The patient presented with melena and progressive anemia, and endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, which could be indicative of a malignant tumour.
The patient has a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction, and the tumour has recurred after resection, which could be indicative of a GIST.
The patient presented with melena and progressive anemia, and has a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with iron deficiency anemia.
The patient presented with melena, and endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, which could be indicative of a gastric ulcer.
The patient had a lipoma resected, but endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, which could be indicative of a lipoma recurrence.
